([[Putnam, Connecticut]]) | college = * [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] (2022–2024) * [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]] (2024–2025) * [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]] (2025–2026) | draft_year = 2026 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 53 | draft_team = [[Houston Rockets]] | career_start = 2026 | years1 = {{nbay|2026|start}}–present | team1 = [[Detroit Pistons]] | years2 = [[2026–27 NBA G League season|2026]]–present | team2 = →[[Motor City Cruise]] | highlights = * [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] All-Defensive team (2026) }} '''Ugonna Kingsley Onyenso''' {{Audio|Ig-Ugonna Kingsley Onyenso.ogg|Listen|help=no}} (born 25 September 2004) is a Nigerian [[basketball]] player for the [[Detroit Pistons]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Motor City Cruise]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]], [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State Wildcats]] and [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia Cavaliers]]. He has also played for the [[Nigeria men's national basketball team|Nigeria national team]], where he was the youngest player to ever play for the team at age 17. Onyenso was selected with the 53rd overall pick in the [[2026 NBA draft]] by the [[Houston Rockets]], traded to the [[New York Knicks]], then subsequently acquired by the Detroit Pistons. == Early career == Born in [[Owerri]], Onyenso played football as a kid before a local coach proposed playing basketball to him.{{Cite web |date=2022-02-26 |title=Ugonna Kingsley Onyenso: The journey so far |url=https://afroballers.com/ugonna-kingsley-onyenso-the-journey-so-far/ |access-date=2022-08-02 |website=Afroballers |language=en-US}} Kingsley was a student-athlete at the [[NBA Academy Africa]] in [[Thiès]], Senegal, where he played for three years.{{Cite news |last=Abayomi |first=Tosin |date=2022-08-02 |title=D'Tigers star Kingsley Onyenso signs for Kentucky |url=https://www.pulse.ng/sports/other-sports/ugonna-kingsley-onyenso-joins-kentucky-wildcats/xxnm9l0 |access-date=2022-08-02 |newspaper=[[Pulse Nigeria]]|language=en}} In January 2021, he moved to the United States to play for the Putnam Science Academy in [[Putnam, Connecticut]]. With Putnam, Onyenso averaged 13.2 points, 9.2 rebounds and 2.7 blocks per game as the team went 20–0 during his tenure there.{{Cite web |date=2022-08-26 |title=Ugonna Onyenso |url=https://ukathletics.com/roster/ugonna-kingsley-onyenso/ |access-date=2023-03-23 |website=UK Athletics |language=en-US}} In August 2021, he also played for Team England of the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU). He played in the 2022 NBA Academy Games and averaged 13.2 points, 9.2 rebounds and 2.7 blocks per game. == College career == On August 2, 2022, Onyenso committed to [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], choosing them over [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]] and [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma]].{{Cite web |last=Tristan |first=Pharis |date=2022-08-01 |title=5-star center Ugonna Kingsley commits to Kentucky |url=https://www.aseaofblue.com/2022/8/1/23269407/ugonna-kingsley-kentucky-basketball-2022-recruits |access-date=2022-08-02 |website=A Sea Of Blue |language=en}} He played sparingly as a freshman. Onyenso missed the first month on his sophomore season with a foot injury but averaged 3.6 points, 4.8 rebounds and 2.8 blocked shots per game. Following the season, he entered the [[2024 NBA draft]] before withdrawing and transferring to [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]].{{cite news |last=Drummond |first=Cameron |title=After planning to turn pro, former Kentucky player Ugonna Onyenso transfers to a new school |url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article287944175.html |access-date=December 20, 2025 |work=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]] |date=June 4, 2024}} Onyenso averaged 2.8 points, 2.4 rebounds and 0.9 blocks per game for Kansas State. He entered the transfer portal again after the season, ultimately landing at [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]].{{cite news |last=Franciulli |first=Jacquie |title=Kansas State center Ugonna Onyenso will transfer to Virginia |url=https://247sports.com/college/virginia/article/kansas-state-center-ugonna-onyenso-will-transfer-to-virginia--249172078/ |access-date=December 20, 2025 |work=247 Sports |date=April 30, 2025}} Onyenso averaged 6.5 points and 4.9 rebounds per game in 36 games. He was named to the [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] All-Defensive team.{{cite news |last=Berman |first=Mark |title=Virginia Tech's Lawal, UVa's Onyenso could go in 2nd round of NBA Draft |url=https://roanoke.com/sports/college/basketball/virginia-tech-hokies/article_15e1e1fb-23b3-4bc3-9a61-a096b3d1689a.html |access-date=June 25, 2026 |work=The Roanoke Times |date=June 23, 2026}} ==Professional career== On June 24, 2026, Onyenso was selected by the [[Houston Rockets]] with the 53rd overall pick in the [[2026 NBA draft]], afterward was traded to the [[New York Knicks]], and lastly to the [[Detroit Pistons]] for cash considerations. He was later signed to a [[two-way contract]] with the Pistons.{{cite web |last=Davis |first=Coty |title=Pistons trade into second round to draft center Ugonna Onyenso |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2026/06/24/ugonna-onyenso-virginia-center-drafted-by-pistons-at-no-53/90687030007/ |publisher=The Detroit News |access-date=25 June 2026}}{{cite web |title=Ugonna Onyenso, Pistons Agree To Two-Way Deal|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/286524/Ugonna-Onyenso-Pistons-Agree-To-Two-Way-Deal|website=realgm.com|date=July 2, 2026|last=Scott|first=Michael|agency=HoopsHype}} == National team career == In November 2021, Onyenso was selected for the [[Nigeria men's national basketball team|Nigeria national senior team]] by coach [[Julius Nwosu]]. In his debut, he scored 10 points, four rebounds and two blocks in 16 minutes against [[Uganda men's national basketball team|Uganda]].
